assumptions.name: Dedicated small-launch price per kg
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: 12 M EUR for 700 kg is about 19000 USD/kg; Electron earns about 28000 USD/kg

assumptions.name: Payload fill rate per launch
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: No public data; a single 200 kg customer fills only about 30% of a launch

assumptions.name: Price per Spectrum launch
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Not published; estimates 10–15 M EUR; NewSpace Index about 10 M USD; Electron earns 8.5 M USD for a third of the capacity

assumptions.name: Rideshare price per kg
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: SpaceX list price 2027; about 10000 USD/kg with separation system

assumptions.name: US government demand open to Isar
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: NSPM-17 sends US government payloads to US-built launchers

assumptions.name: Other governments' demand open to Isar
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Japan, India, Korea and others mostly fly their own launchers

assumptions.name: Heaviest satellite Spectrum can carry to SSO
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Spectrum carries 700 kg to SSO; 1000 kg is its LEO figure and a possible upgrade under ESA Launcher Challenge component B

assumptions.name: Launch sites
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: 0 = Andøya only (Q1 today); 1 = plus Nova Scotia (45–98° from 2028); 2 = plus Kourou (low inclinations and GTO)

assumptions.name: Spectrum launches per year
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Isar's plan for 2027 as its first full operating year; one launch in 2026; production is the bottleneck

assumptions.name: Share of the serviceable market that buys a dedicated launch
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Measured 2025: 6.7% of SAM satellites (4.2% of mass) flew on a small launcher, all on Rocket Lab's Electron; the rest rode SpaceX rideshare. BryceTech: 10–14% in the West. Planet: new rockets get demo payloads first

assumptions.name: Launch success rate
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Insurance of about 25% on Isar's next mission implies 75%; mature launchers reach 92–95%

assumptions.name: Base year of flown demand
assumptions.question: Q1
assumptions.rationale: Latest full year; 2024 as comparison shows how much a single year swings

assumptions.name: Market growth outside megaconstellations
assumptions.question: Q2+
assumptions.rationale: Novaspace forecast implies about 9% a year; BryceTech history 13–17%

launch_sites.name: Andøya Spaceport
launch_sites.isar_access: Exclusive pad 1 for up to 20 years (since April 2021)
launch_sites.note: Licence for the whole spaceport: 30 launches a year, at most 4 at night; headings 280–360°. A second pad is in Norway's 2027 budget proposal; further operators reportedly want to launch from 2027/28 (team research, source to add)

launch_sites.name: Guiana Space Centre (Diamant site)
launch_sites.isar_access: Isar among the Diamant laureates (term sheet 2022); pad retrofit contract not yet submitted
launch_sites.note: Reaches low inclinations and GTO as well as polar orbits

launch_sites.name: Spaceport Nova Scotia (Canso)
launch_sites.isar_access: Dedicated complex signed: 112.5 M USD over 10 years plus 2 × 5 years option
launch_sites.note: Up to 40 launches a year by 2029 (target); inclination range as claimed by the operator
